picks.name: The Pet Parent
picks.why_plausible: Brief is a kitten-focused box with food samples and a care booklet; this persona has affinities for pet_food, pet_supplies, pet_health and subscription_boxes with low-medium price sensitivity. They treat pets as family, which matches the emotional 'first three months' framing.
lean_into: emotional connection with a new kitten
guidance on what to expect in the first months
curated for cats specifically, not generic pet stuff
picks.ad_angle: Give your new kitten the right start: a box built around their first three months of development.

picks.name: The Busy Parent
picks.why_plausible: Time-poor dual-income parents with pet_food and convenience affinities often adopt a kitten for the kids and want one decision made for them. Medium price sensitivity fits a $45 box.
lean_into: time-saving: everything the kitten needs shows up monthly
family-friendly, kids get toys to play with the kitten
avoid: complicated onboarding or long ingredient deep-dives
picks.ad_angle: The whole family wanted a kitten; this box means nobody has to figure out what to buy.

picks.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
picks.why_plausible: Heavy subscription user who defaults to whatever is easiest, and the brief is subscription-only with a fixed three-month run. Urban mid-to-high income at a $45 price point fits their $55 AOV.
lean_into: subscription perks and automatic monthly delivery
picks.ad_angle: Sign up once and the kitten essentials just arrive — no pet-store trips, no guesswork.

picks.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
picks.why_plausible: The brief flags a gift occasion and this persona is female-leaning, family-product oriented, and responds to bundles and clear value. A $45 bundle of toys, food samples and a booklet is easy to articulate as value.
lean_into: clear value: toys, food samples and a guide bundled in one box
reviews from other new cat owners
bundle framing versus buying pieces separately
picks.ad_angle: A ready-made gift for someone who just brought a kitten home — everything bundled in one box.

plan.summary: The only true pet subscription publisher is a direct competitor, so the plan rests on two pet-retail tests — Ruffco for scale and Pawline for subscription-ready owners — with everything else excluded as off-category.

test.name: Ruffco
test.adjustment_reason: Notes call it the 'Largest pet audience in the catalog' with 'repeat-purchase behavior' at 62M impressions, so even a thin slice of new-kitten buyers is a meaningful volume of qualified traffic the category score undervalues.
test.rationale: Ruffco is the biggest pet reach available and its food/pharmacy mix means shoppers are actively provisioning a new animal, which is exactly when a kitten starter box lands; broad 25-55 demographics keep the kitten-owner segment addressable at scale.

evidence.quote: Largest pet audience in the catalog. Broad demographics, repeat-purchase behavior

test.risk: Ruffco already sells pet food and supplies, so kitten owners may feel they have provisioning covered; the audience is also heavily dog-weighted, so cat-specific creative is essential.

test.name: Pawline
test.rationale: Pawline is 'Subscription-heavy' with owners who are 'health-conscious about pets', so the audience is already comfortable with recurring pet billing and with food-sample-led value props.

evidence.quote: Subscription-heavy. Owners are health-conscious about pets, responsive to premium positioning

test.risk: Only 4.8M impressions and a 30-55 skew that leans older than new-kitten adopters; a $45 box may read as cheap to an audience 'responsive to premium positioning'.

bid_strategy.rationale: $45 first order (assumed) × 0.60 = $27.00 target CPA: subscription revenue repeats, so a first order can be bought at a larger share of its value. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: Assumed a first order of about $45, since no price was given.
Assumed a broad adult audience of roughly 25-45, since the brief names no gender or age.
Assumed the box is sold only as a subscription, based on the wording.
Allowable CPA is 60% of first order value (subscription); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
Target CPA is based on an assumed order value. Confirm price before launch.
